item.title: 【AI4S】 Filter By:
item.description: Oral hygiene is fundamental to systemic health, yet toothbrushing, the most common preventive practice, remains largely unguided and unquantified, contributing to the global burden of oral diseases. Current smart toothbrush systems fundamentally fail to capture the critical fine-scale biomechanics at the bristle-tooth interface, which is essential for evaluating clinical adherence and preventing gingival damage. Here we present DigiDent, an AI powered sensing to interpretation system that renders brushing micro-biomechanics computationally interpretable by measuring in-situ contact dynamics at bristle-tooth interface with an embedded E-Bristle sensor. DigiDent fuses bristle-level contact sensing with inertial sensing through a dual-stream neural inference architecture, converting contact-rich brushing behavior into quantitative and interpretable metrics of force, duration, contact-motion pattern, and fine-grained coverage. In validation experiments, DigiDent achieved >99% recognition of motion-contact patterns and 99.84% classification accuracy across 21 brushing subregions. Pilot user-operation verification further demonstrates the feasibility of DigiDent for real-use brushing

item.description: The development of semantic imaging signs is time-consuming and relies heavily on clinicians’ experiential knowledge, whereas the abundance of quantitative radiomic features often poses challenges in interpretability and clinical translation. We developed an agentic AI pipeline to autonomously translate quantitative morphological features into semantic signs. The pipeline autonomously performed end-to-end processing—from descriptive statistical profiling and semantic sign translation to visualization. In a development dataset of 106 supratentorial glioblastoma (GBM) cases, the pipeline generated eight candidate signs; the three most consistently proposed signs were the cauliflower, eggplant, and pancake signs. Two radiologists independently validated the cauliflower sign on an external cohort of 50 GBMs and 50 metastases, achieving AUCs of 0.73 (95% CI: 0.64–0.82) and 0.77 (95% CI: 0.69–0.85), respectively (mean 0.75) for tumor differentiation. item.description: IFPRI’s five decades of experience has shown that development policy research has a stronger likelihood of making an impact and meeting real-world needs when it is adapted to local contexts and created with national and local partners. The best bet for generating context-specific research is operating within beneficiary countries and communities. Building on this evidence, the new IFPRI Strategy 2026-2030 deepens an institutional commitment to decentralization.
